newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland govt signs Korea Zinc agreement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland govt signs Korea Zinc agreement.

text.p: The Queensland state government said on Thursday it has signed a new heads of agreement enabling construction of the planned A$1 billion Korea Zinc refinery to start early next year.

Queensland premier Rob Borbidge signed the agreement with Sun Metals Corporation and Korea Zinc Co Ltd, supplementing an earlier agreement entered into between the previous Queensland Labor government and Korea Zinc.

The agreement follows the introduction into state parliament on Wednesday of the Townsville Refinery Bill and paves the way for construction of the refinery to start after the next North Queensland wet season, Borbidge said in a statement.
The refinery's first stage would involve investment of about A$500 million in a smelter capable of producing 170,000 tonnes of zinc annually with production expected to start in 1999.
Borbidge said the additional agreement would bind Sun Metals Corp to abide by environmental safeguards stipulated in the impact assessment study recently approved by the Queensland government.

The additional agreement also addressed obligations to be met by the companies and the government regarding environmental performance, road access, establishment of a buffer zone and protection of land of cultural heritage significance, he said.

The latest agreement also confirmed the obligation of the companies under the original heads of agreeement to undertake a feasability study for the second stage of the project which included an expansion of the zinc refining capacity and a lead smelter, Borbidge said.
"It will be the first major industrial project in north Queensland in 20 years and will generate almost 600 jobs during construction and 350 jobs during the operational stage," Borbidge said.
